section_summary: This section covers U.S. diplomatic reporting between February 1932 and April 1939 regarding visits, deployments, and maneuvers of Imperial Japanese Navy vessels and aircraft along the coast and inland waterways of China. Consular dispatches and telegrams document fleet movements and displays of military force in treaty ports including Tsingtao, Shanghai, Nanking, Amoy, Chefoo, Foochow, Swatow, and Hankow during periods of heightened Sino-Japanese friction. Major topics include large-scale annual training visits of the Japanese Combined Fleet to Tsingtao, public nationalist speeches by Japanese naval commanders, political maneuvering involving local Chinese leaders such as General Han Fu-chu and Mayor Shen Hung-lieh, and naval activities surrounding the 1932 Shanghai War and 1936 Chengtu incident.

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting the arrival of sixty Japanese naval vessels at Tsingtao.
subfiles.summary: Reports the arrival of sixty vessels of the Japanese Combined Fleet under Admiral Takahashi at Tsingtao, local entertainment plans, and General Han Fu-chu's concurrent inspection visit.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 109: Japanese Navy Arrives in Tsingtao

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum analyzing Admiral Takahashi's nationalist speech at Tsingtao.
subfiles.from: John Carter Vincent (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Analyzes Admiral Takahashi's speech at Tsingtao asserting Japanese rejection of Western superiority and urging overseas Japanese to advance imperial policy.
subfiles.title: FE Memorandum on Admiral Takahashi's Speech

subfiles.about: Despatch forwarding and analyzing Admiral Takahashi's nationalist speech at the Tsingtao Japanese Shrine.
subfiles.summary: Transmits and discusses Admiral Takahashi's speech delivered at a shrine banquet in Tsingtao, which asserted Japanese racial pride, rejected foreign dominance, and called for Japanese leadership in Asia. The dispatch also assesses Chinese political reactions and the significance of General Han Fu-chu's meeting with naval authorities.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 111: Japanese Navy in Tsingtao; Admiral Takahashi's Speech

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting missing aircraft and the rescue of Japanese naval aviators off Shantung.
subfiles.summary: Reports the rescue of two Japanese naval aviators off the Shantung Promontory and notes two carrier planes remained missing after the fleet's departure.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 113: Rescue of Japanese Naval Aviators; Two Planes Missing

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note on Japanese fleet visit to Tsingtao and naval officers visiting Tsinan.

subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.3393/45

subfiles.about: Extract from consular report analyzing the political significance of Han Fu-chu's meeting with Japanese naval commanders.
subfiles.summary: Analyzes General Han Fu-chu's discreet trip to Tsingtao to meet the Japanese naval commander, suggesting efforts to cultivate ties with Japan's naval faction following the Tokyo coup.
subfiles.title: Extract from Tsinan Political Report No. 96

subfiles.about: Extract from consular report summarizing the Combined Fleet's Tsingtao visit and aviation mishaps.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the orderly visit of sixty Japanese warships to Tsingtao, Takahashi's assertive speeches, courtesy exchanges with Han Fu-chu, and the loss of two naval airplanes.
subfiles.title: Extract from Tsingtao Despatch No. 115

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note announcing the upcoming visit of sixty Japanese warships to Amoy.

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting Japanese Yangtze River gunboat deployments and conditions following the Chengtu incident.

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting the annual visit of the Japanese fleet and air maneuvers over Tsingtao.
subfiles.summary: Reports the visit of 60 to 70 Japanese warships to Tsingtao, marked by extensive demonstrations of naval air power, carrier operations, and an alleged maneuver-related citywide blackout.
subfiles.title: Despatch: Visit of Japanese Navy to Tsingtao
